Read a point cloud file

Source: R/point-readers.R
read_points_3d.Rd

Reads LiDAR and photogrammetry point clouds into a data frame with one row per point, ready for geom_point() with aes(z = z) in coord_3d(), or for surface reconstruction with stat_implicit_fit_3d() and stat_alpha_shape_3d(). The reader is chosen by file extension from a registry of native parsers.

Usage

read_points_3d(path)

Arguments

path

Path to a .ply, .las, .xyz, .pts, .txt, .gltf or .glb file.

Value

A data frame with columns x, y, z and the point attributes.

Details

  • PLY (ASCII, binary little- or big-endian): the vertex element; faces, if any, are ignored. red, green, blue (and alpha) become colour; every other scalar property is kept as a column, so normals (nx, ny, nz) and the parameters of 3D Gaussian splatting files (f_dc_0, opacity, scale_0, rot_0, ...) come through by name.

  • LAS 1.0 to 1.4, point formats 0 to 10: coordinates with the header's scale and offset applied, intensity, return_number, number_of_returns, classification, scan_angle_rank (formats 0 to 5, degrees) or scan_angle (formats 6 to 10, degrees), user_data, point_source_id, gpstime where the format records it, and colour and nir where it records them. Names follow lidR's columns in snake case. Compressed LAZ files are read by lidR (lidR::readLAS(), then ggplot2::fortify()).

  • XYZ and PTS text: whitespace, comma or semicolon separated columns, one point per line; a PTS file may start with the point count. Three columns are x, y, z; four add intensity; six add colour when the last three are integers in 0 to 255 and normals nx, ny, nz otherwise; seven add intensity and colour. Further columns are kept as v4, v5, and so on.

  • glTF 2.0 (.gltf, .glb): the points of point primitives (mode 0), placed by their node transforms, with COLOR_0 as colour.

Scanning apps on phones and tablets with a LiDAR sensor (iPhone and iPad Pro models) export PLY, LAS, XYZ or glTF point clouds. Most of them write y-up coordinates; draw those with coord_3d(up = "y").

References

LAS Specification 1.4 (ASPRS), maintained at https://github.com/ASPRSorg/LAS. PLY (Turk): https://paulbourke.net/dataformats/ply/. Kerbl, Kopanas, Leimkuehler, Drettakis (2023). 3D Gaussian splatting for real-time radiance field rendering. ACM Transactions on Graphics 42(4), 139. doi:10.1145/3592433

See also

read_mesh_3d() for meshes.

Examples

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".xyz")
set.seed(1)
u <- runif(400, 0, 2 * pi); v <- acos(runif(400, -1, 1))
writeLines(paste(cos(u) * sin(v), sin(u) * sin(v), cos(v)), path)
pts <- read_points_3d(path)
ggplot2::ggplot(pts, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, colour = z)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point() +
  coord_3d()
